Free French and British forces attempt a landing at Dakar , French West Africa; Vichy French naval forces open fire sporadically for two days, and the expedition is called back.

The Tripartite Pact is signed in Berlin by Germany, Italy, and Japan, promising mutual aid. An informal name, "Axis", emerges.
The first " Liberty Ship ", the SS Patrick Henry is launched. Liberty Ships will prove to be major parts of the Allied supply system.
The National Liberation Front (EAM) is founded in Greece.

10-04.text: The French forces retreat from the Saarland in Germany, and return behind the Maginot Line .
Adolf Hitler and Benito Mussolini meet at the Brenner Pass to discuss the prospects in the war.

10-06.text: Polish resistance in the Polish September Campaign comes to an end. Hitler speaks before the Reichstag , declaring a desire for a conference with Britain and France to restore peace.

10-08.text: in a major victory the Chinese army inflicts heavy losses to the Japanese at Changsha forcing them to retreat to Yueyang.

British civilians are still being killed by German bombs though the attacks have dropped off significantly.
Germans attempt another drive toward Moscow as the once muddy ground hardens.

Draft registration begins in the United States.

10-19.text: Portions of Poland are formally inducted into Germany; the first Jewish ghetto is established at Lublin .

10-23.text: The seized freighter City of Flint reaches Murmansk in the Soviet Union . Here the prize crew is forced to leave the ship, but the latter is not given permission to leave.
Adolf Hitler meets with Franco at Hendaye , near the Spanish-French border; little is accomplished, and least of all Hitler's hope to convince Franco to enter the war on the Axis side.

10-30.text: The British government releases a report on concentration camps being built in Europe for Jews and anti-Nazis.
President Roosevelt, in the middle of an election campaign, promises not to send "our boys" to war.
Franklin Delano Roosevelt approves US$1 billion in Lend-Lease aid to the Soviet Union.

10-31.text: As Germany plans for an attack on France, German Lieutenant-General Erich von Manstein proposes that Germany should attack through the Ardennes rather than through Belgium – the expected attack route.
The United States separates the Corps Areas established in 1921 to perform the administrative tasks of the various regions of the US from the four Field Armies that had been established in 1932.
The Warsaw District government moves all Jews living in Warsaw to the ghettos.
The destroyer USS  Reuben James is torpedoed by Erich Topp 's U-552 near Iceland , killing more than 100 United States Navy sailors. It is the first loss of an American "neutral warship".

11-01.text: Soviet Union annexes the eastern parts of occupied Poland into the Ukrainian SSR and Byelorussian SSR .
Turkey declared neutrality in the Italo-Greek war.
President Franklin D. Roosevelt announces that the U.S. Coast Guard will now be under the direction of the U.S. Navy, a transition of authority usually reserved only for wartime.

11-02.text: The German physicist Hans Ferdinand Mayer compiles, while on a trip to Oslo , the so-called Oslo Report , containing important German secret military information.
The Italian advance into Greece continues. Vovousa is captured and Italian aircraft bomb Salonika .
Political conflict in Yugoslavia as leftists under Tito (Josip Broz) are in competition with the more conservative Serbs under Draža Mihailović .

11-06.text: Sonderaktion Krakau : In Krakow, Nazis detain and deport university professors to concentration camps.

11-08.text: Hitler escapes a bomb blast in a Munich beerhall, where he was speaking on the anniversary of the Beer Hall Putsch of 1923. British bombers coincidentally bomb Munich.
The Battle of Elaia–Kalamas ends and the Italians end their futile offensive in Greece.

11-12.text: The Czech student Jan Opletal dies as a result of wounds inflicted by German authorities, causing vast anger and resentment among Czechs.

11-14.text: The Polish government-in-exile moves to London .

11-15.text: Jan Opletal's funeral sparks new demonstrations in Prague against the police.
The Soviet Union is invited to join Tripartite Pact and to share in the spoils of British Empire. Warsaw's Jewish ghetto is cordoned off from the rest of the city.

Liverpool Blitz : A massive overnight bombing raid results in the Durning Road tragedy

11-30.text: The Soviet Union attacks Finland in what would become known as the Winter War .
A large bombing raid on Southampton in southern England; the city is hit again the next night, followed by Bristol on 2 December, and Birmingham on the 3rd.

12-01.text: Russia continues its war against Finland; Helsinki is bombed . In the first two weeks of the month, the Finns retreat to the Mannerheim line , an outmoded defensive line just inside the southern border with Russia.
Bombing raids are exchanged throughout the month between Germany and Britain. First Germany bombs, then Britain.

12-04.text: The British battleship HMS Nelson is incapacitated for six months by yet another magnetic mine left this time by the U-52 off Loch Ewe .

12-05.text: The Russian invaders begin heavy attacks on the Mannerheim line. The Battles of Kollaa and Suomussalmi begin.
The RAF bombs Düsseldorf and Turin.
Germans call off the attack on Moscow, now 11 miles away; the USSR counter-attacks during a heavy blizzard.

12-07.text: Italy, Norway and Denmark again declare their neutrality in the Russo-Finnish war. Sweden proclaims "non-belligerency", by which it could extend military support to Finland, without formally taking part in the war.

12-11.text: The Russians are met with several tactical defeats inflicted upon them by the Finnish Army.

12-12.text: The escorting destroyer HMS Duchess sinks after a collision with the battleship HMS Barham off the Mull of Kintyre in the North Channel with the loss of 137 men.
In North Africa, over 39,000 Italians lost or captured in Egypt.

12-27.text: The first Indian troops arrive in France.
Operation Archery : British and Norwegian commandos raid the Norwegian port at Vågsøy .

Temperatures fall further on the Moscow front; heavy snows follow and immobilize German tanks.

Large German air-raids on London; St Paul's Cathedral is damaged.

11-07.text: It becomes clear that Ireland will refuse to allow the United Kingdom to use its ports as naval bases.
Heavy RAF night bombings of Berlin, the Ruhr, and Cologne, but with heavy losses.

01-01.text: 10,000 Japanese troops launch a counter-attack in eastern Shanxi Province in China in an attempt to relieve the nearly-surrounded Japanese 36th Division.

01-02.text: The Soviet offensive in Finland is halted by several Finnish victories; numerous Soviet tanks are destroyed.
German bombers bomb Ireland for the second night in a row.

01-10.text: Mechelen incident : a German plane, carrying plans for Fall Gelb , crashes in neutral Belgium.

01-16.text: Captured documents reveal Hitler's plans for the invasion of Scandinavia and a postponement of the invasion of France and the Low Countries until the spring, when the weather is more compatible for an invasion.

01-17.text: The Soviets are driven back in Finland and retaliate with heavy air attacks.

01-20.text: German submarine U-44 torpedoes and sinks Greek steamer Ekatontarchos Dracoulis off Portugal at 04:15, killing 6. U-44 had been hunting for Ekatontarchos Dracoulis for the past 6 hours.

01-21.text: A U-boat sinks British destroyer HMS  Exmouth and its crew of 135 are all lost.

01-24.text: Reinhard Heydrich is appointed by Göring for the solution to the "Jewish Question".
British forces in Kenya continue the East African counter-offensive, attacking Italian Somaliland .

01-27.text: Germany makes final plans for the invasion of Denmark and Norway.

02-01.text: The Japanese Diet announces a record high budget with over half its expenditures being military.
Admiral Husband Kimmel is appointed the Commander of the US Navy in the Pacific.

02-09.text: Erich von Manstein is placed in command of German XXXVIII (38) Armour Corps, removing him from planning the French invasion.

02-10.text: USSR agrees to supply grain and raw materials to Germany in a new trade treaty.
Malta's critical period: now through March, it is under heavy daily attack.

02-14.text: British government calls for volunteers to fight in Finland.

02-16.text: British destroyer HMS  Cossack forcibly removes 303 British POWs from the German transport Altmark in neutral Norwegian territorial waters, sparking the Altmark Incident .

02-21.text: General Nikolaus von Falkenhorst is placed in command of the upcoming German invasion of Norway.
German forces move through Bulgaria toward the Greek front.

03-01.text: Adolf Hitler directs his generals in planning the invasion of Denmark and Norway.

03-03.text: Soviets begin attacks on Viipuri , Finland's second largest city.

03-05.text: Finland tells the Soviets they will agree to their terms for ending the war. The next day they send emissaries to Moscow to negotiate a peace treaty.

The Yugoslav cabinet resigns in protest against Prince Paul's pact with the Nazis. Street demonstration occurs, expressive of a deep dislike for Germany.

03-28.text: Britain and France make a formal agreement that neither country will seek a separate peace with Germany.

02-19.text: The start of the "three nights Blitz" of Swansea , South Wales . Over these three nights of intensive bombing, Swansea town centre is almost completely obliterated.

02-20.text: German and British troops confront each other for the first time in North Africa—at El Agheila in western Libya.

03-07.text: First British troops land in Greece, at Piraeus.

03-08.text: Another bombing of London, notable because Buckingham Palace is hit.

03-09.text: The Italian Spring Offensive in the Albanian front begins.

03-13.text: The Luftwaffe strikes with a large force at Glasgow and the shipping industry along the River Clyde .

03-19.text: The worst bombing of London so far this year, with heavy damage from incendiary bombs; Plymouth and Bristol are bombed again.

03-20.text: The Italian Spring Offensive is called off, after heavy losses and virtually no progress.

03-24.text: Rommel attacks and reoccupies El Agheila , Libya in his first offensive. The British retreat and within three weeks are driven back to Egypt.

03-25.text: Italian MTMs of the Decima MAS sink the heavy cruiser HMS  York  (90) , a large tanker (the Norwegian Pericles ), another tanker and a cargo ship in Suda Bay , Crete .

03-31.text: The Afrika Korps continues the German offensive in North Africa; Mersa Brega , north of El Agheila , is taken.

04-02.text: After taking Agedabia, Rommel decides to take all of Libya and moves his troops toward Benghazi. All of Cyrenaica (Libya) seems ready for the taking.

04-07.text: The Luftwaffe begins a two-day assault on Belgrade, Yugoslavia; Hitler is infuriated by the Yugoslav resistance.

04-17.text: Yugoslavia surrenders. A government in exile is formed in London. King Peter escapes to Greece.

04-19.text: London suffers one of the heaviest air raids in the war; St. Paul's is mildly damaged but remains closed; other Wren churches are heavily damaged or destroyed.

04-21.text: With their retreat cut off by the German advance, 223,000 Greek soldiers of the Greek army in Albania surrender.

04-22.text: The British, both military and civilian, begin to evacuate Greece.

04-23.text: Greek government is evacuated to Crete , which Churchill is determined to defend.

04-26.text: Rommel attacks the Gazala defence line and crosses into Egypt; Tobruk continues to hold however.

05-02.text: British forces at RAF Habbaniya launch pre-emptive air strikes against Iraqi forces besieging them and the Anglo-Iraqi War begins.

05-03.text: British forces in Ethiopia begin the investment of Amba Alagi where Italian forces under the Duke of Aosta have taken up defensive positions.

05-04.text: Belfast, Northern Ireland, experiences another heavy bombing by the Luftwaffe.

05-14.text: The RAF is authorized to act against German aircraft in Syria and on Vichy French airfields.

05-15.text: First Civilian Public Service camp opens for conscientious objectors in the United States.

05-16.text: Rommel defeats a counter-attack, "Brevity", at Halfaya Pass. The two sides trade alternating control of Fort Capuzzo and Halfaya Pass.

05-17.text: British forces in the Habbaniya area advance on Iraqi-held Fallujah and, in five days fighting, push the Iraqis out.

05-18.text: The Duke of Aosta, Viceroy of Italian East Africa, surrenders his forces at Amba Alagi.

05-22.text: Iraqi forces unsuccessfully counter-attack the British forces in Fallujah and are rebuffed.

05-26.text: In the North Atlantic, Royal Navy Fairey Swordfish aircraft from the carrier HMS  Ark Royal fatally cripple the Bismarck in torpedo attack.

05-29.text: Members of the German military mission flee Iraq.

06-02.text: Tuskegee Airmen begin with the formation of the 99th Fighter Squadron.

06-06.text: More British fighter planes are delivered to Malta; Luftwaffe attacks continue.

06-08.text: Vichy French-controlled Syria and Lebanon are invaded by Australian, British, Free French, and Indian forces.

06-15.text: British Operation Battleaxe attempts and fails to relieve the Siege of Tobruk . The British are heavily defeated at Halfaya Pass nicknamed "Hell-fire pass".

06-21.text: President Roosevelt authorizes $6,000 For Executive Order 8807 (Manhattan Project-Nuclear Weapons).

07-07.text: British and Canadian troops in Iceland are replaced by Americans.

07-13.text: Montenegro starts an uprising against the Axis Powers shortly after the Royalists in Serbia begin theirs. Questionable Communist plans instigate parallel uprising and civil war.

07-17.text: Luftwaffe air attacks on Malta continue.

07-19.text: The " V-sign ", displayed most notably by Churchill, is unofficially adopted as the Allied signal, along with the motif of Beethoven's Fifth Symphony .

07-20.text: Heinrich Himmler visits Soviet POWs near Minsk and Lublin and decides to build the concentration camp near Lublin known as Majdanek concentration camp .

07-21.text: The Luftwaffe strikes heavily at Moscow.

08-05.text: German armies trap Red Army forces in Smolensk pocket and take 300,000 soldiers; Orel is taken.

08-07.text: Germans reach the Gulf of Finland , cutting the Soviet forces in Estonia into two, with the forces in Tallinn being detached from the rest of Soviet lines.

08-09.text: Franklin D. Roosevelt and Winston Churchill meet at NS Argentia , Newfoundland . The Atlantic Charter is created, signed, and released to the world press.

08-12.text: Hitler, against the advice of his generals, shifts some forces from the Moscow front to Leningrad and the Crimean offensives.

08-20.text: German 250th Infantry Division, nicknamed "Blue Division" and consisting of Spanish volunteers, was formed and began to move to Poland.

08-28.text: German forces with the help of Estonian volunteers take Tallinn from the Soviets. The Soviet evacuation from the city inflicts heavy casualties with more than 12,000 dead and dozens of ships sunk in Finnish and German mi

09-04.text: USS  Greer becomes the first United States warship fired upon by a German U-boat in the war, even though the United States is a neutral power. Tension heightens between the two nations as a result. The U.S. is now c

09-10.text: German armies now have Kiev completely surrounded .

09-11.text: Franklin D. Roosevelt orders the United States Navy to shoot on sight if any ship or convoy is threatened.

09-16.text: Reza Pahlavi , Shah of Iran is forced to resign in favour of his son Mohammad Reza Pahlavi of Iran under pressure from the United Kingdom and the Soviet Union.

09-19.text: German capture of Kiev is now formal. The Red Army forces have suffered many casualties in defending this chief city in Soviet Ukraine.

09-26.text: The U.S. Naval Command orders an all-out war on Axis shipping in American waters.

10-05.text: German forces capture Saaremaa island in Estonia from the Soviets.

10-27.text: German Army Group South forces reach Sevastopol in the Crimea, but the tanks of the "Northern" forces are slowed or stopped entirely by mud.

10-29.text: Vilna Ghetto II liquidated. 2,500 Jews killed.

11-04.text: Hirohito approves the attack on Pearl Harbor.

11-18.text: Operation Crusader : British Commonwealth and other Allied troops cross into Libya and at least temporarily relieve the Siege of Tobruk .

12-03.text: The last Soviet outposts in Estonia ( Osmussaar island ) and in Finland ( Hanko Naval Base ) are evacuated to Kronstadt .

12-10.text: British battlecruiser HMS  Repulse and battleship HMS  Prince of Wales are sunk in a Japanese air attack in the South China Sea.
